Scholarship_Name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation College Scholarship Program
Eligibility: An undergraduate scholarship program available to high-achieving high school seniors with financial need who seek to attend the nation’s best four-year colleges and universities.

Open to under-resourced students ages 16-24 who will be high school seniors by October 1, 2025. Applicants must be permanent residents of CO, DC, FL, KY, MA, NJ, NM, NC, OH, RI, NH, UT, or TX. Must be Pell-eligible or demonstrate financial need and plan to attend a 4-year accredited college in their home state as an incoming freshman.

Open to graduating high school seniors from the 2025-26 academic year who have participated in an approved college readiness program for their junior and senior years. Applicants must have a minimum 2.4 GPA, demonstrate financial need, be eligible for a Federal Pell Grant, and be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Must plan to enroll in a full-time bachelor's degree program in the fall immediately following graduation.

Organization: National Society of High School Scholars (NSHSS)
Eligibility: Available to first-generation college students. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to expanding diversity and inclusion initiatives in their school, community, or workplace. Selection is based on academic merit, an educator recommendation, and an essay.
Applicants must be a high school senior or current undergraduate student who is the first in their family to attend college or university.

Scholarship_Name: Minority Women in STEM Financial Need Scholarship
Eligibility: Must be a BIPOC female undergraduate student studying a STEM major and demonstrating financial need. Applicants must be attending one of the following Texas universities: University of Texas at Dallas, University of Texas at Austin, University of North Texas, The University of Texas at Arlington, Texas Woman's University, or Texas A&M University- College Station.

Available to full-time students of Hispanic/Latino heritage residing in the Tri-State Region. Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, pursuing a degree in business, with a minimum GPA of 3.0, and demonstrated financial need.
Any low-income Hispanic or Latinx high school senior in New York may apply for this scholarship.
Must be an underrepresented minority undergraduate student attending an HBCU and majoring in a STEM field. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 or higher and be involved in their communities.

Scholarship_Name: Carl N. and Margaret Karcher Founders Scholarship
Eligibility: Must be a graduating high school senior or graduate planning to attend college for the first time as a full-time student. Applicants must be 26 years of age or younger and reside in one of the 16 states where Carl's Jr. operates. Winners demonstrate leadership in their communities and extracurricular activities. First-generation students are encouraged to apply.

Scholarship_Name: SCFU Scholarship for HBCU Business Students
Eligibility: Eligible applicants are undergraduate and graduate students currently enrolled in business-related majors at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). Applicants should be committed to driving social change and economic empowerment through their careers in business.

Open to any undergraduate student pursuing a four-year degree at an HBCU. Applicants must be majoring in business or agriculture and have a GPA of 2.7 or higher. The scholarship aims to support students by reducing the expenses of tuition and books.
Categories: Merit, STEM, Heritage, Community Service, Minority, Need-Based

Eligibility: An undergraduate scholarship program available to high-achieving high school seniors with financial need who seek to attend and graduate from the nation's top four-year colleges and universities.
Open to female high school seniors and undergraduate students from a low-income household who are pursuing a degree in a STEM field.
Open to female-identifying high school seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA who are planning to pursue a degree in engineering. Applicants must have prior non-profit or volunteering experience.
Categories: Merit, STEM, Women, Community Service, Leadership, Minority

Eligibility: Open to high school seniors, four-year undergraduate, or graduate students pursuing a career in healthcare or the physical sciences. Applicants must have a GPA of 3.0 or higher, demonstrate financial need, and have a deep passion for Heavy Metal music.

Scholarship_Name: Kinesiology Leadership/Community Service Scholarship - UM Eastern Shore
Eligibility: Available to students at the University of Maryland, Eastern Shore, who are studying kinesiology, exercise science, or a related field. Applicants must demonstrate exceptional leadership and community service.

Any community service-oriented undergraduate or graduate student who has non-profit or volunteering experience may apply. This scholarship seeks to honor the legacy of Priscilla Shireen by supporting students who share her devotion to service.
Categories: Community Service, Women, Minority, Merit, Need-Based

Eligibility: Must be a high school junior or senior residing in Ohio. Applicants must have volunteering or community service experience. The scholarship is intended for introverted students who are actively involved in making a positive impact on their communities.

Scholarship_Name: Fine and Performing Arts Scholarship - University of Evansville
Eligibility: Available to incoming freshmen who plan on majoring in art, music or theatre at the University of Evansville. Selection is based on the applicant's high school record.

Scholarship_Name: Arts and Music Scholarship - Rhodes College
Eligibility: Available to entering freshmen at Rhodes College. You must plan to major or minor in art, music, or theatre to be eligible for this award.
Open to high school seniors and undergraduate students from Illinois who plan to pursue a major in the performing arts, such as music, theater, or dance. Selection criteria include ambition and need.

Open to high school seniors with a disability or special needs who participate in sports. Applicants must reside in an East Coast state (ME, NH, MA, RI, CT, NY, NJ, DE, MD, VA, NC, SC, GA, FL, VT, PA, WV, DC) and plan to pursue post-secondary education or training.

Available to high school seniors who have participated in sports. Selection is based on outstanding athletic ability and performance, academic aptitude and achievements, and school leadership and community service.

Scholarship_Name: Rev. Herman A. Martin Memorial Scholarship
Eligibility: Must be a high school senior residing in Arkansas with a minimum GPA of 3.0. The scholarship aims to assist students in furthering their education.

Any undergraduate or graduate student who is passionate about sports and pursuing a career in a sports-related field may apply. Applicants should be committed to building a future in the industry and have a clear vision for their professional future.
